Rashi on Nedarim 62a:10:1.hebrew: אלא קשיא דיר' טרפון - אם שרי ליה לאיניש לאודועי נפשיה שהוא חכם במקום שאין מכירין אותו, אמאי ציער נפשיה בשביל שהודיע לזה שהוא חכם:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:10:1.english: But [there is] a difficulty [from the case] of Rabbi Tarfon - If it is permitted for a person to make himself known that he is a Sage in a place where they do not recognize him, why did he distress himself because he informed this [man] that he was a Sage?

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:12:1.english: Resolve my case - Advance my case before those of others for the honor of my Torah [learning].

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:12:2.hebrew: ובני דוד כהנים היו - אלא מה וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:12:2.english: And the sons of David were priests - [They were not actual priests;] rather, just as [a priest takes first,] etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:1:1.english: [They] are permitted with regard to stealing - Because the owners have despaired of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:1:2.english: And [they] are exempt from the tithe - Because they are ownerless [property].

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:2:1.english: Their owner - The owner of the figs.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:2:2.english: And they were folded, etc. - For [they] are permitted for any person to eat.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:2:3.hebrew: משום סניות מילתא - כלומר, מרוע לב היה אומר כן, ולא משום עין יפה, דעדיין לא הפקירן:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:2:3.english: Due to the odiousness of the matter - That is to say, he was saying this out of ill will and not out of generosity, for he had not yet declared them ownerless.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:4:1.hebrew: אשכחיה - לרבי טרפון גופיה דקאכיל מן התאנים, דקסבר דהפקירא נינהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:4:1.english: He found him - Rabbi Tarfon himself, who was eating from the figs, for [Rabbi Tarfon] thought that they were ownerless.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:4:2.hebrew: אחתיה - לר' טרפון בשקא, ההוא גברא שהיה משמרן:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:4:2.english: He placed him - [He placed] Rabbi Tarfon in a sack — that man who was guarding them [the figs].

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:4:3.english: Over this matter - That he saved himself through the honor of his Torah, in that he said, "Woe to Tarfon."

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:5:1.english: Robbers - who took [the vessels] out of the Temple.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:5:2.english: And they became non-sacred - And even so, Belshazzar was killed on account of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:1.hebrew: אמאי ציערו - ההוא גברא לר' טרפון? הא מהפקירא קא אכיל:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:1.english: Why did he trouble him - [that is, why did] that man [trouble] Rabbi Tarfon? Behold, he was eating from ownerless [produce].

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:2.english: And he thought: This is [the one] who stole from me - For this reason he troubled him.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:3.hebrew: אי הכי אמאי ציער ר' טרפון נפשיה - כיון שתפסו כגנב, מאי הוה ליה למעבד:
Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:3.english: If so, why did Rabbi Tarfon berate himself - Since [that man] seized him as a thief, what could he have done?

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:6:4.english: He should have appeased him - With money.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:9:1.english: For their Maker - For the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:9:2.english: And speak of them for the sake of Heaven - That all your intention should be for [the sake of] Heaven.

Rashi on Nedarim 62a:9:3.english: To hoe, etc. - To earn a livelihood from it in order to eat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:12:1.english: Resolve my dispute - That is to say, adjudicate my lawsuit first.

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:1:1.english: [If most of the knives] have been set aside, etc., [they] are permitted with regard to stealing - Because the owners declare them ownerless.

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:1:2.english: And [they] are exempt from the tithe - [they are] like ownerless property.

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:4:1.english: That I made use of the crown of Torah - For that man left him [alone] out of respect for his Torah [learning].

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:6:1.hebrew: [א"ה אמאי ציער] - מאי הוה ליה למיעבד, כיון שלא היה רוצה להניחו בענין אחר? בשלמא אי הוה שביק ליה כי אמר "הוקפלו רוב המקצועות", ניחא, שהיה מצטער על מה שלא אמר לו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:6:1.english: [If so, why did he berate] - What could he have done, since [that man] did not want to leave him alone in any other way? It would be understandable if [the man] would have let him go had he said, "Most of the knives have been set aside" — [then] it would make sense, for he would have been distressed over not having told him [that].

Tosafot on Nedarim 62a:7:1.english: "To love the Lord your God" - [This] implies [doing so] out of love for the Creator, and not for your own honor.
